title: From Taxi Driver to Famous Fishing Fly Maker
main_content:
Elpheus Ndlovu has come a long way from his village in the South African province of Mpumalanga. He once worked as a taxi driver. Now, he makes fishing flies – artificial, man-made flies that are used to catch fish. The flies he now ties are used all over the world by fishers to make record-breaking catches.

A man tests a fishing reel in the Fly-Fishers Unlimited store in Johannesburg. Next to him is a quiet man in his 40s. Elpheus Ndlovu is affectionately known as ‘Alphons’ in the fly-fishing community.

Elpheus Ndlovu uses both natural materials, such as bird feathers, and artificial ones, like plasti. His goal is to make flies look like real creatures – insects, frogs, minnows and crabs – that fish feed on.

Elpheus Ndlovu likes to remember the day back in 1994 when he saw the newspaper advertisement that changed his life.

While making fishing rods, he met the owner of Fly-Fishers Unlimited, Murray Pedder, who taught him to how tie flies.

Instead of a job, Elpheus ‘Alphons’ Ndlovu has found a job that has enabled him to buy a house and to educate his four children.
